cloze.s: The artist spent weeks painting a ___ of the mayor, getting her face and smile just right.

why: old cloze gave the answer away ('National Portrait Gallery') and its claim that a painted portrait of every president hangs there was unverified

set.note: In a constitutional monarchy, such as Sweden or Spain, the king or queen is mostly a symbol and elected leaders govern.

why: Japan has an emperor, not a king or queen

ex: Millions of soldiers died in World War I, many in muddy trenches in France and Belgium.
Sofia's great-great-grandfather drove an army ambulance in France during World War I.

why: US Army Nurse Corps was women-only in WWI; 'grandfather served as an army nurse' was historically doubtful
fiction's def (made-up stories) overlaps novel's for (a)/(b)
novel overlaps fiction's def; autobiography is nonfiction, a near-opposite for (f)
rhyme also means verse/a short poem (near-synonym for (e)); 'known for fiction inspired by jazz' fits the Langston Hughes cloze
equality (same rights and treatment for all) overlaps 'rules applied fairly to all'
'the law guarantees justice before the court' also fills the cloze; defs overlap
free will ('choices genuinely your own') and human rights ('basic freedoms') overlap 'freedom to act as you choose'
argument ('reasons given to support a conclusion') overlaps logic's def
democracy is a near-opposite of monarchy (ant: republic) for (f)
'shared millions of times on (the) internet' can fill the cloze
'the interest on Hannah's loan/mortgage kept growing' also fills the cloze
dictatorship reads as a near-opposite for the opposite question (ant: censorship)

set.note: Older mobile phones that mainly make calls and send texts are often called basic phones or feature phones.

why: 'flip phone' names a shape, not a type; several current smartphones fold and flip
